title: I Enforced the Shuffleboard-Court Clock on the League Who Overstayed

parts.text: I booked court two at 2:16 p.m. and the league still had discs on my numbered wax. The board said: ONE COURT. SIXTY MINUTES. CLEAR THE DISCS. I was fifty-one, rec player, holding a permit. Captain Rhee shrugged. "Leagues are the wax." I photographed the board, the permit, and their discs on my time. Then I asked for the court log. At 2:22 rec staff pinged why Rhee's name was on overtime wax. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: Rec staff can see Rhee's discs on court two during my sixty.

social.video_title: The league left discs on my numbered wax — Part 1/2
social.description: Shuffleboard, a sixty-minute board, league discs. I logged overtime. Would you have asked for the court log?

parts.text: Rhee called it a hammer until rec asked for the still. I printed the log, the board, and the photo. The discs cleared. Rhee booked the next sixty and told the league hammers were always about optics. Optics is a word captains use when wax exists. Clock policy now has a second line: LEAGUES CLEAR THE DISCS. I keep my sixty. Rhee schedules. The court finally looks like a permit, not leftover wax. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.description: Court log, cleared wax, and a second line. Was a hammer ever my permit?
